title: Anomalous stabilization of excitons by metallic proximity
authors: Jeongkeun Song, Uksam Choi, Shan Lin, Du Li, Baekjune Kang, Li Yang, Ambrose Seo, Changhee Sohn, Ho Nyung Lee
abstract: Metallic environments are generally expected to suppress excitons through strong dielectric screening, yet their influence can differ in composite systems where metallic and insulating regions coexist. Here, we investigate excitonic states in PdxCu1-xCrO2 thin films across a percolation-driven metal-insulator transition. Optical spectroscopy and many-body GW calculations show that CuCrO2 hosts strongly bound excitons with a binding energy of about 489 meV. With increasing Pd substitution, the system approaches an insulator-to-metal transition near x = 0.5, consistent with the site-percolation threshold of a triangular lattice. In the pre-percolation regime, the excitonic resonance redshifts by 241 meV while the Tanguy continuum onset remains nearly unchanged, consistent with a substantial increase in exciton binding energy before metallization. An image-charge-based excitonic hydrogen model shows that isolated metallic regions can enhance electron-hole binding through image-charge interactions, whereas conventional screening is recovered once a continuous metallic network forms. Although this model provides a possible interpretation of the observed excitonic evolution, an alternative scenario in which metallic and excitonic responses originate from electronically distinct states and evolve independently cannot be excluded. These results reveal unusual metallic-excitonic coexistence near a percolation-driven metal-insulator transition and suggest nanoscale metallic proximity as a possible route for modifying excitonic interactions.
summary: This paper investigates how excitons behave in $	ext{Pd}_x	ext{Cu}_{1-x}	ext{CrO}_2$ thin films near a metal-insulator transition. Contrary to expectations, isolated metallic patches enhance exciton binding energy via image-charge interactions before the material becomes fully metallic. This suggests that nanoscale metallic proximity can be a powerful tool for engineering excitonic properties.
main_problem: The paper investigates the anomalous stabilization of excitons in insulating materials when they are in close proximity to metallic regions, challenging the conventional view that metals always suppress excitons via dielectric screening.
main_result: The study shows that in the pre-percolation regime, isolated metallic regions enhance electron-hole binding energy through image-charge interactions, leading to an increase in exciton binding energy before the continuous metallic network forms and causes screening.
method: The research combines optical spectroscopy (measuring the dielectric function) with many-body GW–BSE calculations and employs an image-charge-based theoretical model to quantify the electrostatic interactions.
model_or_system: The system studied is $	ext{Pd}_x	ext{Cu}_{1-x}	ext{CrO}_2$ thin films, which undergo a percolation-driven metal-insulator transition. The theoretical model uses an image-charge perturbation Hamiltonian to describe the interaction between excitons and isolated metallic inclusions.
key_observables: Exciton binding energy ($E_b$), redshift of the excitonic resonance peak ($E_1$), and the dielectric function ($\varepsilon_2$).
important_parameters: Percolation threshold ($x \approx 0.5$), separation distance ($D$) relative to exciton size ($a_X$), and the Pd concentration ($x$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the system can be modeled as a heterogeneous composite, and the enhancement mechanism is dominated by local image-charge interactions when metallic regions are isolated.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the systematic redshift and monotonic increase in $E_b$ as Pd doping approaches the percolation threshold, contrasting this enhancement with the quenching observed once a continuous metallic network forms.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical system and the problem (exciton stability vs. metal proximity). It presents experimental evidence of the percolation transition and the anomalous enhancement of $E_b$ in the pre-percolation regime. Finally, it uses an image-charge model to theoretically explain this enhancement mechanism.
why_interesting: The work provides a concrete example of how local, nanoscale electronic structure (image-charge effects) can override bulk screening predictions, offering a tunable mechanism for controlling excitonic properties in hybrid quantum materials.
